question.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2t+1 \\ y=3-t \\ z=t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2t+1 \\ 3-t \\ t+2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ -t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(1,3,2)$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
